title: MTH1W — Financial Literacy + Data Management Mosaic

questions.text: Noah invests $3,000 at an annual simple interest rate of 4.5% for 8 years. How much **interest** will they earn?

commonErrors.feedback: Did you convert the % to a decimal? r = rate/100. So 5% → 0.05.
Just the **interest** is asked for — not the total. I = P × r × t, not P + Prt.
Check the units of t. If the rate is per year, t should be in years.

questions.text: After 6 years of simple interest at 5.5%/year, Noah's account has earned $264.00 in interest. What was the original **principal** invested?

commonErrors.feedback: Rearrange I = Prt to solve for P: P = I / (r × t).
Convert % to decimal before plugging in: r = rate/100.

questions.text: Cameron invests $2,000 at 5%/year, compounded **annually**, for 6 years. What is the total amount in the account at the end?

commonErrors.feedback: Compound interest grows by the factor (1+r) raised to t, not multiplied by t.
Compounded **annually** means n = 1. Formula simplifies to P(1+r)^t.

questions.text: Dakota deposits $2,500 at 6%/year, compounded **quarterly**, for 6 years. How much will the account be worth at the end?

commonErrors.feedback: n is the number of times interest compounds per year. Monthly = 12, quarterly = 4, semi-annually = 2.
The exponent is n×t (total number of compounding periods), not just t.

questions.text: Dakota bought a home for $400,000. Real estate in the area is appreciating at 5% per year (compounded annually). What will the home be worth after 15 years?

commonErrors.feedback: Appreciation uses (1 + r). If you used (1 − r), you depreciated instead of appreciated.
Exponential growth uses (1+r)^t. Linear growth uses V₀ + d·t. Check which model the question asks for.

questions.text: Cameron bought a new car for $45,000. It depreciates at 18% per year (compounded annually). What is the car worth after 2 years?

commonErrors.feedback: Depreciation uses (1 − r). If you used (1 + r), you appreciated instead.

questions.text: Quinn bought a piece of land for $120,000. It appreciates by **$2,000 per year** (linear growth). What will it be worth after **8 years**?

commonErrors.feedback: Linear appreciation ADDS a fixed amount each year: V = V₀ + d·t. Not (1+r)^t.
Appreciation INCREASES, so add. V = V₀ + d·t.

questions.text: Christian earns $3,500 per month after tax. Their monthly expenses are: rent $1168, food $413, transportation $352, other $561. How much can Christian put into **savings** each month?

commonErrors.feedback: Savings = Income − total expenses. Make sure you SUBTRACT, not add.

questions.text: Liam earns $2,400 per month and spends $302 on transportation. What **percent** of Liam's monthly income goes to transportation? (Round to 2 decimal places.)

commonErrors.feedback: Percent of income = (amount / income) × 100, not (income / amount) × 100.

questions.text: Kendra sees a sweater originally priced at **$24.99** marked **30% off**. What is the **sale price**?

commonErrors.feedback: Looks like you found the discount AMOUNT. Sale price = original × (1 − pct/100), or original − discount.
A discount REDUCES the price. Use (1 − pct/100), not (1 + pct/100).

questions.text: Uma takes out a $10,000 car loan at 7% per year (compounded monthly) over 5 years. What is their **monthly payment**?

commonErrors.feedback: r in the loan formula is the MONTHLY rate, not annual. r = annual/100/12.
n is total number of monthly payments. n = years × 12.

questions.text: Grace wants to buy a phone. **Option A:** pay **$1,500** upfront. **Option B:** pay **$95/month for 18 months**. **How much more** does Option B cost than Option A?

commonErrors.feedback: The question asks the DIFFERENCE (how much MORE), not the sum. Compute Option B total − Option A total.
Compute total for BOTH options, then subtract. Option A = cash price. Option B = monthly × months.

questions.text: A student records these test scores: 5, 6, 9, 13, 22. What is the **median**?

questions.text: The data set is: 10, 16, 25, 27, 35, 45, 46. What is the **range** of this data?

questions.text: The data set is: 2, 14, 16, 21, 28, 33, 38, 49. What is the **interquartile range (IQR)**? (Q1 = median of lower half, Q3 = median of upper half, IQR = Q3 − Q1.)

commonErrors.feedback: IQR ≠ range. IQR = Q3 − Q1 (Q1 = median of lower half, Q3 = median of upper half).

commonErrors.feedback: Appreciation uses (1 + r). If you used (1 − r), you depreciated instead of appreciated.
Exponential growth uses (1+r)^t. Linear growth uses V₀ + d·t. Check which model the question asks for.

questions.text: Xavier bought a new car for $45,000. It depreciates at 12% per year (compounded annually). What is the car worth after 8 years?

commonErrors.feedback: Depreciation uses (1 − r). If you used (1 + r), you appreciated instead.

questions.text: Sophia bought a car for $40,000. It depreciates by **$2,500 per year** (linear depreciation). What is it worth after **7 years**?

commonErrors.feedback: Depreciation DECREASES, so subtract. V = V₀ − d·t.
Linear depreciation SUBTRACTS a fixed amount each year: V = V₀ − d·t. Not (1−r)^t.

questions.text: Maya earns $2,200 per month after tax. Their monthly expenses are: rent $748, food $314, transportation $169, other $300. How much can Maya put into **savings** each month?

commonErrors.feedback: Savings = Income − total expenses. Make sure you SUBTRACT, not add.

questions.text: Emma earns $3,200 per month and spends $414 on food. What **percent** of Emma's monthly income goes to food? (Round to 2 decimal places.)

commonErrors.feedback: Percent of income = (amount / income) × 100, not (income / amount) × 100.

questions.text: Dylan sees a sweater originally priced at **$75.00** marked **40% off**. What is the **sale price**?

commonErrors.feedback: Looks like you found the discount AMOUNT. Sale price = original × (1 − pct/100), or original − discount.
A discount REDUCES the price. Use (1 − pct/100), not (1 + pct/100).

questions.text: Aiden takes out a $25,000 car loan at 6% per year (compounded monthly) over 4 years. What is their **monthly payment**?

commonErrors.feedback: r in the loan formula is the MONTHLY rate, not annual. r = annual/100/12.
n is total number of monthly payments. n = years × 12.

questions.text: Ben wants to buy a phone. **Option A:** pay **$2,000** upfront. **Option B:** pay **$65/month for 36 months**. **How much more** does Option B cost than Option A?

commonErrors.feedback: The question asks the DIFFERENCE (how much MORE), not the sum. Compute Option B total − Option A total.
Compute total for BOTH options, then subtract. Option A = cash price. Option B = monthly × months.

questions.text: A student records these test scores: 3, 8, 16, 21, 24, 25, 27. What is the **mean** (rounded to 2 decimal places)?

commonErrors.feedback: The question asks for the MEAN (average). Median is the middle value.
Mean = sum of values ÷ count of values.

questions.text: A class records these shoe sizes: 8, 7, 21, 8, 18, 19, 11, 8. What is the **mode**?

commonErrors.feedback: The MODE is the value that appears most often. Count occurrences.

questions.text: The data set is: 4, 9, 10, 13, 20, 20, 34, 36. What is the **range** of this data?

commonErrors.feedback: Range = max − min of the whole data set. (IQR would be Q3 − Q1.)

questions.text: The data set is: 3, 9, 13, 16, 32, 42, 44, 44. What is **Q1 (the median of the lower half)**?

commonErrors.feedback: Q1 = median of the LOWER HALF (not the median of the whole data set). Q3 = median of the UPPER HALF.

questions.text: A scatter plot of kilometres driven (x) vs fuel used (L) (y) has line of best fit **y = 2x + 20**. Predict the fuel used (L) when kilometres driven = 6.

commonErrors.feedback: Plug the x value into the equation y = mx + b. Multiply m × x first, then add b.

questions.text: A scatter plot of kilometres driven (x) vs fuel used (L) (y) has a line of best fit passing through **(0, 5)** and **(8, 21)**. **Predict y** when x = 4.

commonErrors.feedback: First find slope m = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁), then b = y₁ − m·x₁, then predict y = m·x + b.
Check the SIGN of your slope — is y rising or falling as x increases?
